02 · how to read these charts

One series identity everywhere; every historical caveat is drawn, not footnoted

Series identityour-data = blue, control = orange on every chart; seed-1 repeats are the same hue, thinner and lighter; the historical run is dashed grey. Colors follow the arm, never the chart. Bands are raw per-iteration min/max envelopes; lines are lightly smoothed (moving average, ~1/120 of the window); hover any chart for exact smoothed values.
Axesx is always transitions (iterations × 500 for smpl, × 1024 for g1; the historical overlay uses the console's exact Total steps). g1 charts use log-x so the 0–512k window shared with the crashed historical run stays readable next to 9.6M; y switches to log only where a channel is strictly positive across several decades (marked “log y”). Chart y-ranges clip to the 1–99th percentile band where warm-up spikes would otherwise flatten the whole run (noted per chart).
Honest limits(i) the shaded warm-up window is not update-for-update comparable: the rsl_rl pin changed the warm-up gate (collected > random + num_envs) — the historical smpl run printed its first FB update at iteration 101, today's pair logs it at 100 (schedule-class delta, never a method verdict); (ii) FB losses are not monotone quality proxies — quality lives in sections 04/06; (iii) channels existing on only one side are labeled on the chart.

06 · g1 quality at the pilot horizon

Tracking breaches on the original gauge; the reference-free reward gate lands 1.397× in our favor

Reference-free broad-reward gate (receipts/rewardgate_20260806/)

25.83ours · B1 mean return, 38 reward tasks × 10 episodes (2026-08-06)
18.49control · B2 mean return, same regenerated dataset, same protocol
1.397×B1/B2 aggregate return ratio ≥ 0.909 → PASS — the only reference-free policy-quality measurement in the ladder
Reference-free parity confirmed (2026-08-06): the our-data arm returns 1.40× the control on the shared 38-task broad-reward measure — no task-level quality deficit; this closes the abdiag residual (“our smoother references might just be easier targets”) in the our-data arm's favor at pilot scale. Heterogeneity recorded: median per-task ratio 0.806, B1 better on 16/38 — the arms trade task families (B1: spin-arms 18.3×, rotate-z 12.4×; B2: raisearms 6.1×, sitonground 2.2×), and B1 buys returns with more action (l2 +0.51) and auxiliary penalty (+2.47). Both arms miss the frozen phase-2 anchor (0.34×/0.47×) under recorded caveats (regenerated dataset + known stack-class delta) — per the standing decision rule, anchor deltas are never method verdicts.
